Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as soon as possible :PostDoc (m/f/d) in Data-Driven Social Ecological Research(Full-Time / Part-Time ** ** options available)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: Full-Time; Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, limited to 3 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.SBiK-F has strong cooperations with the Institute for social-ecological research (ISOE) and the position will work closely with both institutions.The position develops quantitative approaches to (1) better characterize and measure human–nature interactions, or (2) use these analyses to identify leverage points for more effective stewardship or monitoring of nature under climate change.Your tasks- Develop quantitative approaches to measure and analyze human–nature interactions- Integrate multiple data streams (ecological, social, remote-sensing, citizen-science) into coherent models of social-ecological system dynamics- Identify leverage points where intervention or monitoring most effectively supports biodiversity- Advance biodiversity or stewardship monitoring frameworks to better incorporate social dimensions- Publish in leading international journals- Contribute to and connect with ongoing research at SBiK-F- Collaborate across the natural- and social-science groups at Senckenberg, ISOE, and partner institutionsYour profile- PhD in ecology, environmental science, quantitative social science, or a related field- Demonstrated experience working with empirical ecological data and preferably also social data- Strong proficiency in R (and/or comparable statistical/programming environments)- Excellent quantitative and statistical skills- Strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals- Fluency in written and spoken EnglishDesirable skills- Experience with integrating heterogeneous data streams (eg. ecological, social, remote sensing or citizen science data)- Familiarity with AI/ML methods- Track record of interdisciplinary collaboration across natural and social sciences- Experience in quantitative social science methods and working with social or socio-economic data- Experience in acquiring third-party funding- Familiarity with trait-based approaches to social-ecological questions- Familiarity with adaptive capacity and resilience of social-ecological systems- Familiarity with impacts of climate change on the interactions between biodiversity and societyWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV with full publication list, copies of certificates and diplomas, along with the names of two referees), electronically (as a single PDF) stating the reference: #11-26026 by 29.11.2026.Please submit your application via our online application system. If you are viewing this vacancy on an external job platform, please visit our careers page and apply via the corresponding "Apply" button. Candidates with HVDC, offshore wind, or high-voltage infrastructure experience are highly preferred.Your Tasks- Coordinate and supervise maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, and commissioning activities on offshore HVDC converter platforms.- Manage OEMs, contractors, and service providers while ensuring efficient execution of offshore works.- Ensure compliance with HSE requirements, Permit-to-Work systems, LOTO procedures, and electrical safety standards.- Monitor work progress, technical quality, schedule adherence, and compliance with project requirements.- Coordinate interfaces between operations, engineering, commissioning, HSE teams, and contractors.- Track technical defects, non-conformities, and outstanding works while preparing site reports and escalating critical issues.- Assume VEFK (Responsible Electrical Person) duties where formally appointed.Your qualifications- Technician, Master Craftsman, or equivalent qualification in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, or a related discipline.- Experience within offshore wind, HVDC/HGÜ systems, substations, high-voltage installations, or energy infrastructure projects.- Strong knowledge of HV/MV equipment, electrical isolation procedures, LOTO, and Permit-to-Work systems.- Experience in site supervision, contractor coordination, maintenance, and/or commissioning activities.- VEFK qualification or solid experience within the German electrical safety framework is highly desirable.- Good understanding of HVDC converter systems and reactive power compensation systems is an advantage.- Strong HSE mindset, proactive approach, and ability to work independently.- Good English skills; German language skills are considered beneficial.- Willingness to work offshore, travel regularly, and participate in standby rotations.- Offshore medical fitness and offshore safety certification (or willingness to obtain them).

jobs.description: Your TasksAs a System Engineer Predevelopment you will play a key role in shaping the earliest phases of cutting‑edge satellite missions. In this role, you will lead platform‑level system engineering activities during Phase A/B1, orchestrate technical inputs from expert teams and subcontractors, and help define the mission and system architecture. You will contribute to laying the technical, programmatic, and schedule foundations that ensure mission success through the entire development lifecycle.Tasks:- Support the Lead System Engineer for the Phase A/B1 study.- Coordinate technical inputs from specialist engineering departments and individual subcontractors.- Execute trade‑offs and analyses to define the mission and system architecture.- Lead the parts of the platform and subsystem system design as an architect, including deriving and maintaining requirements from satellite to subsystem level.- Support Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) activities for the mission.- Contribute to the assessment of the satellite development approach to ensure the target Technology Readiness Level (TRL) by the end of Phase B1.- Support the definition of the overall project breakdown structure (Work Breakdown Structure) for phases B2, C/D, and E1 through in‑orbit commissioning.- Assist in developing the programme plan for the satellite across phases B2, C/D, and E1 up to in‑orbit calibration and validation.- Support the creation of a project implementation schedule for the platform, aligned with the overall programme planning.Analyse and assess potential cost drivers for the platform.- Support the identification and evaluation of technical and programmatic risks, including cost, schedule, and feasibility drivers.- Support the definition and implementation of risk mitigation measures for the platform.Your QualificationsMinimum:- Master-level degree in aerospace engineering with a focus on space systems- Knowledge of science, exploration and space safety space missions- Competencies in space mission design, satellite systems engineering and spacecraft subsystem design- High level of flexibility, willingness to work in international teams and ability to keep tight schedules- High motivation, pro-active working approach and strong sense of responsibility- Excellent communication, presentation and documentation skills- Fluency in both spoken and written (business) EnglishIdeal:- Industry experience in space system engineering- Knowledge of requirements engineering for subsystems of space systems and preparation of specifications- Experience in Model Based Systems Engineering- Fluency in German language

We are seeking an experienced Grid Connection Engineer to support offshore wind projects with a strong focus on grid compliance, power system studies, and technical integration. The role requires hands-on experience with grid connection engineering, stakeholder management, and compliance verification according to German grid codes and TSO requirements. Previous experience with offshore wind developers is considered a key advantage.Your Tasks- Review and validate power system models using DIgSILENT PowerFactory, PSCAD, or similar simulation tools.- Manage and oversee subcontractors performing grid connection, conformity, and design studies.- Prepare and review ONAR, NAR, and other grid compliance studies and supporting documentation.- Assess turbine, converter, PPC, and network models to ensure compliance with project and operational requirements.- Identify compliance gaps, perform technical investigations, and develop corrective solutions through calculations and simulations.- Define and verify interfaces between TSO, PPC, SCADA systems, and other project stakeholders while ensuring alignment with VDE-AR-N 4131 and grid connection requirements.Your qualifications- Degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems Engineering, or a related discipline.- Proven experience in offshore wind projects, ideally on the developer side.- Strong expertise in grid compliance studies, including ONAR, NAR, VDE-AR-N 4131, and TSO requirements.- Advanced knowledge of DIgSILENT PowerFactory, PSCAD, or comparable power system simulation software.- Solid understanding of PPC, SCADA systems, plant control concepts, and grid connection interfaces.- Excellent stakeholder and interface management skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple technical parties effectively.- Fluency in english is required
